label: Duality: Points and Cameras
notes: This chapter runs across printed pages 502 to 514 and develops Carlsson-Weinshall duality. The headline is simple and surprising: once we fix a projective basis of reference points, scene points and camera centres become interchangeable objects, so any theorem about cameras viewing points has a free dual about points viewing cameras.

label: Why Duality Helps
notes: Motivate the chapter by the payoff. Minimal-data reconstruction results are scarce and hard to derive twice. Duality lets us prove one and transport it. Resectioning and triangulation, the six-point and seven-point problems, turn out to be two readings of the same algebra once the reference basis is fixed.

label: The Reduced Camera
notes: Everything rests on the reduced camera. Choosing four world basis points that map to the four image basis points strips a general camera down to four free parameters a, b, c, d on the diagonal. In this frame the projection equation becomes a symmetric template that we can read in two directions.

label: The Symmetric Product
notes: Walk through the central identity. The reduced projection of a point has entries aX+dT, bY+dT, cZ+dT. The same three numbers arise when a reduced camera assembled from the point coordinates acts on the parameter vector a,b,c,d. That coordinate-level symmetry is the engine of the whole duality.

label: Interchanging the Roles
notes: Now state the interchange cleanly. A configuration of N cameras and M points maps to a dual configuration of M cameras and N points, with centres and points swapping seats. The image measurements are preserved as incidences, so a solvable primal problem guarantees a solvable dual problem of swapped dimensions.

label: Incidence Is the Invariant
notes: Stress what actually survives the swap. The scalar l-transpose P X is symmetric in point and camera data, and equals the back-projected plane acting on the point. Image lines through a measured point back-project to planes meeting along the camera ray. Incidence, not metric structure, is what duality preserves.

label: Canonical Image Frames
notes: Explain the first algorithmic step. In every view we pick four image points and apply a projective transformation sending them to the canonical image basis e1, e2, e3 and the centroid e4. This is legal precisely when no three anchors are collinear, and it makes the reduced template apply view by view.

label: The Dual Algorithm
notes: Describe the bookkeeping. After canonicalizing, drop the four special rows, transpose the remaining m-by-n measurement block, and append four synthetic rows carrying e1 through e4. Those synthetic rows force the dual solution to use reduced cameras. Solve the dual reconstruction, then map the answer back to the original problem.

label: Resectioning Meets Triangulation
notes: Make the duality tangible with the flagship example. Resectioning, finding a camera from known points, is dual to triangulation, finding a point from known cameras. Under the swap one algorithm services both, and counting arguments for one problem immediately yield the minimal-data count for its dual.

label: The Reduced Fundamental Matrix
notes: Specialize to two views. A reduced fundamental matrix has already absorbed the four synthetic correspondences e_k to e_k, so its diagonal and its total sum vanish, leaving five free parameters. Each extra same-image dual correspondence adds one linear equation, which is what makes the six-point dual algorithm work.

label: The Reduced Trifocal Tensor
notes: Extend to three views and seven points. A neat small parametrization is not available, so the safe pattern is constrained least squares: synthetic correspondences give exact linear constraints C t equals zero, and real correspondences give a data term minimized inside that nullspace. This delivers the seven-point dual result.

label: Conditioning and Takeaways
notes: Close on the practical caveat and the summary. Canonicalizing with nearly collinear anchors is geometrically legal but numerically dangerous, inflating the homography condition number and distorting noise. Recap: fix the basis, exploit the symmetric template, swap points and cameras, and reuse one reconstruction result as two.
